newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-JOHNSON AND AFZAAL GUIDE NOTTS TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JOHNSON AND AFZAAL GUIDE NOTTS TO VICTORY.

text.p: An unbroken fifth-wicket stand of 160 between captain Paul Johnson and Usman Afzaal guided Nottinghamshire to a six-wicket win over Lancashire in an English championship match at Old Trafford on Saturday.
Lancashire took the initiative on the final morning with fast bowler Peter Martin taking three early wickets to leave Nottinghamshire on 64 for three, still needing another 156 for victory.
But Johnson, adding to his 66 in the first innings, and Afzaal, who took his match aggregate to an unbeaten 147, turned an apparently evenly-balanced game decisively in the visitors' favour.
Elsewhere, former England opener Bill Athey found an ally in the afternoon rain to help him save Sussex from defeat against Somerset at Taunton.

Athey grafted to a 215-ball century which included 13 fours, and was still at the crease on 138 when play was abandoned with Sussex on 259 for five in their second innings, 91 runs ahead of Somerset's imposing first innings total of 409.
Sussex had started the day in trouble on 142 for three, still needing 26 runs to make the home side bat again.
Defending champions Leicestershire recorded their first win of the new campaign by beating strugglers Hampshire at Southampton.
Leicestershire, who started the day on 31 without loss, moved on to 119 for the loss of five wickets for a relatively comfortable victory.
Glamorgan beat Kent by 87 runs and Essex beat Durham by 125 runs in the day's other two championship matches.
